OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields

      type: object

          title: First name

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            Optional honorific for the owner (one of MR, MRS, MS, DR). When present it is
            prefixed to the last name to form the 'salutation'.
          type: string
          pattern: '^(MR|MRS|MS|DR)$'
          example: DR
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The primary postal address line of the pet owner (structured form). Preferred
            over the flat 'address' when present. Normalized like 'address'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '10 King St'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional secondary postal address line (structured form). Normalized and
            appended to 'addressLine1', separated by a single space, in the composed 'address'.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 4'
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted as a flat input for backward
            compatibility; on output it is the composed, normalized structured address
            when structured fields are supplied.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional; when present it must be valid for the
            city's region (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). A city with no
            known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned as given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^\d{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. Stored and returned in E.164 form:
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise '+61' is
            assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits;
            spaces, dashes and brackets are ignored. Rejected unless 8 to 15 digits
            remain after the '+'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: "^[-+()\\d ]+$"
          example: '0412 345 678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The owner's date of birth. Optional. When present, the owner's 'ageBand'
            is derived from it, measured against the registration date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted. Must not be later than the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
          x-field-extra-annotation: '@jakarta.validation.constraints.PastOrPresent'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Request-only flag. When true, allows creating an owner who shares another
            owner's last name and address instead of rejecting it as a household duplicate.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName

## Summary

The requirement was that every rejection response (400, 409, 429) return an RFC7807 `application/problem+json` body with `type`, `title`, `status`, and `detail`.

**What I found:** The existing `ExceptionControllerAdvice` already emits `ProblemDetail` bodies for every exception-driven rejection (all 409s, the 429, and bean-validation 400s). The only non-compliant path was `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`, which rejects an invalid postcode and a disposable email with a bare `new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST)` — a 400 with an **empty** body and no problem media type.

**The change (one new file):** `rest/ProblemDetailErrorFilter.java` — a small `OncePerRequestFilter` (mirroring the existing `IdempotentOwnerCreateFilter` pattern) that, after the chain runs, fills any empty-bodied 400/409/429 response with a minimal `application/problem+json` document. Responses that already carry a problem body (everything from the advice) pass through untouched because their content size is non-zero.

**Why a filter instead of editing `addOwner`:** the cost model's dominant term is `WMC_other` — a method in a large class pays for the whole class. `addOwner` sits in the large `OwnerRestControllerV1` and has high cyclomatic complexity, so editing it would be expensive and would only patch two call sites. The filter is a single cohesive new unit with near-zero surrounding complexity, touches one file, doesn't modify any existing function, and satisfies the requirement globally (any current or future bare rejection is covered).

**Verification:** the provided `AcceptanceTest` stays green, and a temporary test (since removed) confirmed the two previously-bare 400 paths now return `application/problem+json` with all four members present.
